newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1996 platinum demand seen lower.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1996 platinum demand seen lower.

text.p: Japanese platinum demand for calendar 1996 is expected to fall slightly, due mainly to a sharp drop in demand from the investment sector and a moderate decline from the autocatalyst sector, Johnson Matthey PLC, the world's leading platinum group metals refiner, said on Tuesday.
Johnson Matthey's interim 1996 platinum review estimated Japan's total platinum demand in 1996 at 2.03 million ounces this year, against an actual 2.22 million last year.
Demand from the investment sector would be pressured by a sharp fall in sales of large bars in Japan as yen weakness against the dollar cooled investor interest, the report said.
Demand for platinum in jewellery fabrication would be flat at 1.48 million ounces in 1996 despite a rise in retail sales.

"The slowdown is mainly due to the fact that Japanese jewellery distributors have been reducing their stocks, but we expect the sales of Platinum 1,000 (a high-purity alloy popular in wedding rings and other jewellery items) to continue to rise," said Alison Cowley, an executive at Johnson Matthey's precious metals marketing division.

Retail platinum jewellery demand in the first six months of 1996 was strong, with sales of relatively inexpensive platinum jewellery up by 12 percent from the previous year while sales of platinum pieces costing over 500,000 yen each rose six percent.
Japan's platinum demand from the autocatalyst sector was likely to fall to 255,000 ounces this year from 270,000 last year, the report said.

The decline was attributed to a drop in domestic car output and car exports. Cowley said Japanese cars produced for export tended to have relatively high loadings of platinum in their catalytic converters.
